key_insight: A linear eddy-viscosity closure can regularize the chaotic adjoint Navier-Stokes equations, enabling stable prediction of the mean domain of dependence for wall-stress measurements in turbulent channel flow.
engineering_relevance: This improves the ability to infer past wall-borne flow events from surface sensing, which is important for turbulence diagnostics, flow control, and wall-model-based estimation.
method: Solve adjoint Navier-Stokes equations backward in time from a wall-sensor kernel.
Add a linear eddy-viscosity closure to the ensemble-averaged adjoint equations to mitigate exponential growth.
Compare the predicted mean domain of dependence with ensemble-averaged adjoint realizations and examine Reynolds-number trends.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports direct computation of the mean domain of dependence and comparison against ensemble averages, with universal behaviors observed across Reynolds numbers for wall-stress sensitivity and actuation structures.
watch_item: The closure regularizes only the ensemble-mean adjoint behavior, so individual adjoint realizations remain chaotic and the approach may be sensitive to model assumptions in more complex flows.
paper_title: Mitigating adjoint chaos in wall turbulence
